identity.name: Old Kingdom of Egypt
alt_names: Egypt of the Third to Sixth Dynasties

land.text: the Nile valley and Delta of the Second Dynasty's Egypt

predecessors.note: Page infobox 'Preceded by: Early Dynastic Period'; 'Began: c. 2686 BC'.

land.text: the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut, ruled from Memphis by the Seventh and Eighth Dynasties (c. 2181-c. 2160 BC), then from Heracleopolis

successors.note: First Intermediate Period page: 'Memphis (c. 2181 BC - c. 2160 BC), Seventh Dynasty-Eighth Dynasty'.

land.text: the southern nomes from Elephantine north to about Siut, where 'powerful nomarchs' held local power; the Theban Eleventh Dynasty is dated from c. 2134 BC

successors.note: Only the Thebes core becomes a state (upper-egypt, from -2134); in -2181..-2135 the land is recorded as the nomarchs' own, counterpart 'nobody'.

capitals.name: Memphis (Ineb-Hedj; Mit Rahina)
capitals.note: Page: 'remained at Ineb-Hedj, the Egyptian name for Memphis'; Djoser's pyramid is in Memphis' necropolis, Saqqara.

correction.text: the Nile valley and Delta, 'the Nile River region south to Abu (also known as Elephantine)', as in Cliopatria's Old Kingdom shape, held from c. 2686 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives 'Began: c. 2686 BC' (Djoser, c. 2686 - c. 2649 BC) where Cliopatria starts the Old Kingdom in -2500 and gives -2686..-2501 to the Early Dynastic row. Shape unchanged (it is identical to the Early Dynastic one).

93,286 km2, Elephantine (lat 24.0) to the Delta coast (31.6). The page has no infobox area: it says 'Egypt consisted of the Nile River region south to Abu (also known as Elephantine)' plus Sinai and the western-desert oases, and gives a population of 1.6 million for 2500 BC, so no ratio can be taken. The Sinai mines and oases are not drawn (undated, no extent given).

Identical shape to the previous one. The Sixth Dynasty (2345-2181 BC) 'power of the pharaoh gradually weakened in favor of powerful nomarchs' but the page names no lost or seceded province before the end, so the shape stands.

correction.text: unchanged shape; years extended from -2201 to the page's end of the Old Kingdom, c. 2181 BC

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria ends the Old Kingdom in -2201 and starts Lower and Upper Egypt in -2200; the page gives 'Ended: c. 2181 BC' and dates the Sixth Dynasty 2345-2181 BC, with the last king 'c. 2184 - c. 2181 BC'. The First Intermediate Period page begins the Memphis-based Seventh Dynasty at c. 2181 BC. Shape unchanged, years only.

region.text: 'the Nile River region south to Abu (also known as Elephantine)'

ledger.note: c. 2686 BC: Djoser founds the Old Kingdom (Third Dynasty) at Memphis. Page: 'The first King of the Old Kingdom was Djoser (sometime between 2691 and 2625 BC)'; reign 'c. 2686 - c. 2649 BC'; infobox 'Began: c. 2686 BC'.
2613: the Fourth Dynasty begins, the Old Kingdom's zenith. Page: 'The Fourth Dynasty (2613-2494 BC)', when 'royal power reached a zenith'; Khufu (2589-2566 BC) built the Great Pyramid.
2494: the Fifth Dynasty begins. Page: 'The Fifth Dynasty (2494-2345 BC)'; Sahure's expedition to Punt is dated 2487-2475 BC (trade, no territory).

2345: the Sixth Dynasty begins and royal power starts to slip. Page: 'During the Sixth Dynasty (2345-2181 BC) the power of the pharaoh gradually weakened in favor of powerful nomarchs (regional governors).'

region.text: the southern nomes from Elephantine north to about Siut, left to their nomarchs when the Old Kingdom ended

ledger.note: c. 2181 BC: the south passes to its nomarchs. The pages name no state in the south between c. 2181 and the Theban Eleventh Dynasty (infobox Thebes c. 2134 BC); that the land was held by the provincial governors is the researcher's bridging reading of 'powerful nomarchs (regional governors)'. Cliopatria instead draws an 'Upper Egypt' state from -2200.

region.text: the Delta and Middle Egypt, passing to the Memphite Seventh and Eighth Dynasties

ledger.note: c. 2181 BC: the Old Kingdom ends and the First Intermediate Period begins. Page: 'Ended: c. 2181 BC'; 'Internal disorders set in during the incredibly long reign of Pepi II (2278-2214 BC)'; low Niles 'between 2200 and 2150 BC'. First Intermediate Period page: Memphis (c. 2181-c. 2160 BC), Seventh-Eighth Dynasties.

wars.name: Sixth Dynasty expeditions into Canaan
wars.outcome: No territorial result recorded: the page says only 'At least five military expeditions were sent into Canaan' under the Sixth Dynasty.
wars.note: Years are the Sixth Dynasty's (2345-2181 BC); the page dates none of the expeditions. The page also mentions Nubian and Canaanite expeditions under earlier kings and that Merenre 'sent officials to maintain Egyptian rule over Nubia from the northern border to the area south of the third cataract', all undated and so not drawn.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the kingdom is the Nile valley and Delta, bounded by desert and by Elephantine in the south.

notes: Cliopatria's three rows (-2500..-2301, -2300..-2251, -2250..-2201) are one identical 93,286 km2 shape. Dates follow the page (c. 2686-c. 2181 BC) against Cliopatria's -2500..-2201: the dossier starts 186 years earlier (taking the shape from the Early Dynastic row) and ends 20 years later. CONFLICT WITH CLIOPATRIA: Cliopatria draws Lower Egypt and Upper Egypt as states from -2200; the pages opened show the Memphite Seventh-Eighth Dynasties from c. 2181 BC, the Herakleopolitan kings from c. 2160 and the Theban Eleventh Dynasty from c. 2134, so the south is recorded as 'nobody' in between (confidence 1). NOT DRAWN: the page's 'Nubian control reached north of the third cataract' (an infobox sentence that appears to describe Nubia's, not Egypt's, reach), Sinai and the oases, Sneferu's reach 'from ancient Libya in the west' (undated). The page gives dynasty spans and a few reigns (Djoser, Khufu, Pepi II) but no full list, so no ruler strip.
